prs.title: fix(useComboBox): prevent default on Escape when it closes the popover
prs.author: ayuxy027
prs.body:
Closes #10784

Pressing Escape with the ComboBox popover open closes the popover, but the browser also handles the key. In Safari fullscreen that means Escape exits fullscreen as well.

On the issue it was noted that the Escape shortcut should already prevent the default unless told not to. That default only applies when a shortcut action returns `undefined`: `createKeyboardShortcutHandler` treats `undefined` as `{shouldPreventDefault: true}`, but when the action returns an object it only prevents the default if `shouldPreventDefault` is truthy. The Escape action returns `{shouldContinuePropagation}`, so `shouldPreventDefault` was `undefined` and nothing was prevented.

The fix returns `shouldPreventDefault: state.isOpen` from the Escape action, so Escape that closes the popover is prevented. I kept it in `useComboBox` rather than changing the handler's default for object returns, because that would:

- change every `useKeyboard({shortcuts})` action that returns an object without `shouldPreventDefault`, across the library and in consumers;
- prevent Escape even when the popover is already closed, so a closed ComboBox would swallow Escape for things like Safari fullscreen or a native `<dialog>`.

Propagation is unchanged, so parent dialogs behave as before. Happy to move the change into the handler instead if you'd prefer that.

prs.title: fix(DatePicker): keep the popup time field from collapsing inside a Form
prs.author: costajohnt
prs.body:
Closes #10899

## Summary

A time-enabled S2 `DatePicker` or `DateRangePicker` inside a `Form` shows a collapsed time field in its calendar popup. The popover is portaled, but React context still flows through it, so the popup `TimeField` reads React Aria's `FormContext` from the surrounding form. S2 `TimeField` uses that context to switch on `grid-template-columns: subgrid`, which only makes sense when the field sits directly in the form's grid. In the popup its parent is a flex column, the subgrid resolves to `none`, and the field box shrinks to a few pixels while the segments overflow it.

`CalendarPopover` already clears `OverlayTriggerStateContext` for its children, so it now clears `FormContext` the same way. That fixes both pickers since they share the popover. The picker field itself still reads the form context from outside the popover, so its layout in the form is unchanged.

One side effect: the popup time field no longer inherits the form's `validationBehavior`. With `<Form validationBehavior="aria">`, its min/max errors now commit on blur like they do outside a form. It has no `name` and lives outside the `<form>` element, so form submission and server errors are not affected.

prs.title: fix: double click event from keyboard on some buttons and inputs
prs.author: snowystinger
prs.body:
Closes https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/issues/10658

The general idea is, if the default behaviour of a browser initiated click is fired because of keyboard Space or Enter, then we don't fire an additional click, as that will look like a virtual click and also result in two click events, the real one and the virtual.

prs.title: fix: let a Popover's aria-label take precedence over its trigger label
prs.author: UditDewan
prs.body:
Partially addresses #7240 (the Popover case reported in [this comment](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/issues/7240#issuecomment-2895490555), which was confirmed as a bug). The broader audit of `useLabels` across components is not included here.

## Summary

**Intent:** when a standalone `Popover` (one without a `Dialog` inside, so the popover itself gets `role="dialog"`) is given an `aria-label`, screen readers should announce that label, not the trigger's text.

**Root cause:** `DialogTrigger` (and `MenuTrigger`/`Select`) pass the trigger's id to `Popover` through `PopoverContext` as `aria-labelledby`, so the popover is labelled by its trigger when it has no label of its own. When the user also passes `aria-label`, both attributes end up on the element, and `aria-labelledby` takes precedence in accessible name computation. The result is that "Open products menu" is announced instead of "Products menu".

**Fix:** this follows the existing pattern in `Dialog`, where the context `aria-labelledby` is only a fallback. `Popover` now records the `aria-labelledby` passed via props before merging context. If an `aria-label` is provided and no `aria-labelledby` was explicitly passed, the context-provided `aria-labelledby` is dropped. Explicit `aria-labelledby` props behave as before, and popovers without their own label are still labelled by their trigger.
